## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="b3-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Reading sequence</dt><dd>Sets, parameters, variables, objective, constraints: what is counted, given, chosen, scored and ruled out.</dd>
<dt>Indices and sums</dt><dd>p with indices g and t is a table; Σ over g adds a column, Σ over t a row.</dd>
<dt>Units</dt><dd>$/MWh × MW × h = $: every term of the objective in dollars, with Δt written out.</dd>
<dt>For all</dt><dd>One line with ∀ t ∈ T stands for one row per hour.</dd>
<dt>Verification</dt><dd>Does the model do what its equations say? Units, signs, balance, duals, a hand check.</dd>
<dt>Validation</dt><dd>Is the model right enough for the question? Compare with real data and expert judgement.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Why the balance dual is $0 at 17:00 and $80 at 18:00</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

A [balance dual]{.lx-term term="shadow-price"} is the change in the cheapest total cost when one hour's demand rises by 1 MWh.

- **19:00 and 20:00: \$40.** The combined-cycle plant simply makes 1 MW more.
- **18:00: \$80.** The plant already climbs its full 40 MW from 17:00, so 1 MW more at 18:00 needs 1 MW more at 17:00 too, where it pushes out free wind: \$40 + \$40 = \$80, still below the \$100 peaker.
- **17:00: \$0.** The plan already spills 10 MW of wind and sun to warm the plant up for the evening; one more MWh there just spills less.
- **Linked hours.** The ramp links the hours, so it links their prices. The Modeler lesson M1 reads such duals as marginal values for a whole day.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The objective and the balance in Pyomo</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

Each line of the formulation becomes one line of code, with the sets doing the copying. Here are the objective and the balance in [Pyomo](https://www.pyomo.org/), with `c`, `d`, `V` and `dt` holding the parameters; the sizes, weather, ramp and nuclear lines are left out:

```python
from pyomo.environ import *
m = ConcreteModel()
m.T = Set(initialize=[17, 18, 19, 20])
m.G = Set(initialize=["nuc", "wind", "solar", "cc", "pk"])
m.p = Var(m.G, m.T, within=NonNegativeReals)   # MW
m.u = Var(m.T, within=NonNegativeReals)        # MW
m.cost = Objective(expr=sum(c[g] * m.p[g, t] * dt for g in m.G for t in m.T)
                        + sum(V * m.u[t] * dt for t in m.T))
m.balance = Constraint(m.T, rule=lambda m, t:
    sum(m.p[g, t] for g in m.G) + m.u[t] == d[t])
```

Suspect 3 in code is a single balance row for hour 17, in place of the indexed one:

```python
m.balance = Constraint(expr=sum(m.p[g, 17] for g in m.G) + m.u[17] == d[17])
```

- **Drop `* dt`:** the objective is then right only at one-hour steps.
- **The skill:** reading code against the formulation, line by line, as in this lesson.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Researcher</span>Validation in published energy studies</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

Validating an optimization model is hard: it describes what would be cheapest, not what will happen.

| Approach | Evidence | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| Look back | For the UK's electricity transition from 1990 to 2014, the cumulative cost of the real path deviated by 9 to 23% from the cost-optimal paths of a model, under the study's alternative assumptions ([Trutnevyte, 2016](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.energy.2016.03.038)). | One country and one model; the real path was never meant to be cost-optimal. |
| Good practice | Guidance for energy-system optimization studies asks for documented, verifiable models and for uncertainty to be explored, not hidden ([DeCarolis et al., 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2017.03.001)). | A standard to meet, not a test that passes or fails. |

The Researcher lesson R5 (upcoming) turns both into a routine.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="b3-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="optimal" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A model that solves to ‘optimal’ has passed verification.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. All five suspects solved to optimal. The solver checks the mathematics, not whether it says what you meant.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="neg2" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A balance dual can never be negative.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Here all four are ≥ 0, but when output is forced above demand, more demand saves money: cut 17:00 demand to 105 MW and its dual becomes −$140. Real markets see <span class="lx-term" data-term="negative-price">negative prices</span> for the same reason.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="dt" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Adding up p in MW over the hours gives energy in MWh.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Multiply by Δt first. With one-hour steps the number happens to be the same; at 15-minute steps the plain sum is four times too big.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="b3">

<p class="lx-qtext">A model's cost is far below your hand estimate, and the dearest plant runs first. Which check finds the bug fastest?</p>

<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>The units: a cost in $/kWh read as $/MWh makes a plant look a thousand times cheaper, as suspect 1 showed. The balance still holds.</p></details>

<div class="lx-card b3-pstatic">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Practice: nine exercises in three sets · about 39 min</p>
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, each exercise runs the solver, gives hints one at a time and checks your answer.</p>
<h3>Read a line</h3>
<p>Say what a line means, the unit of every symbol, and how many rows it stands for.</p>
<ol class="b3-ps">
<li><p><b>The ramp line, word by word</b> (worked example, about 2 min)</p>
<p class="b3-static-line">−<i>R</i> Δ<i>t</i> ≤ <i>p</i><sub>cc,<i>t</i></sub> − <i>p</i><sub>cc,<i>t</i>−1</sub> ≤ <i>R</i> Δ<i>t</i> &nbsp; ∀ <i>t</i> ∈ <i>T</i></p>
<ul class="b3-static-worked"><li><b>In words.</b> From one hour to the next, the combined-cycle plant's output changes by at most R, up or down.</li><li><b>Units.</b> p is in MW; R = 40 MW per hour times Δt = 1 h is MW too: every side in MW.</li><li><b>Rows.</b> Two limits per hour, one on each side: 4 hours give 8 rows.</li><li><b>First hour.</b> At t = 17, p(cc, 16) is not a variable but the start, 45 MW: a parameter.</li></ul>
<p>How many rows would this line stand for over a whole day of 24 hours?</p>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Two rows per hour, 2 × 24 = 48.</p></details></li>
<li><p><b>A storage line: the units</b> (partly worked, about 3 min)</p>
<p class="b3-static-line"><i>e<sub>t</sub></i> = <i>e</i><sub><i>t</i>−1</sub> + η <i>q<sub>t</sub></i> Δ<i>t</i> − <i>w<sub>t</sub></i> Δ<i>t</i> &nbsp; ∀ <i>t</i> ∈ <i>T</i></p>
<p>The energy in a battery at the end of hour t is what it held an hour before, plus what charging adds after losses, minus what it discharges.</p>
<ul class="b3-static-worked"><li><i>e<sub>t</sub></i>, energy stored: <b>MWh</b> (given)</li><li>Δ<i>t</i>, the step: <b>h</b> (given)</li></ul>
<p>Give the unit of each: <i>q<sub>t</sub></i>, charging power, η, the share kept, <i>w<sub>t</sub></i>, discharging power. Rows for the 4 hours of T?</p>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>q(t): MW; η: no unit; w(t): MW. MWh = MWh + (no unit × MW × h) − (MW × h), and 4 rows, one per hour.</p></details></li>
<li><p><b>A reserve line, from scratch</b> (from scratch, about 5 min)</p>
<p class="b3-static-line">Σ<sub><i>g</i>∈{cc, pk}</sub> (<i>P̄<sub>g</sub></i> − <i>p<sub>g,t</sub></i>) ≥ <i>r<sub>t</sub></i> &nbsp; ∀ <i>t</i> ∈ <i>T</i></p>
<p>What does this line ask for?</p>
<ol class="b3-static-ch" type="a"><li>Every hour, the two gas plants keep at least r(t) of unused capacity in hand.</li><li>Every hour, the two gas plants make at least r(t).</li><li>Over the whole day, the gas plants' unused capacity adds up to at least r.</li><li>Every hour, each gas plant keeps r(t) unused.</li></ol>
<p>The unit of r(t)? Its rows over a day of 24 hours? Rows of the 24-hour model with this line added?</p>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Every hour, the two gas plants keep at least r(t) of unused capacity in hand. Unused gas capacity in MW, one row per hour; 264 rows for the day plus 24 reserve rows: 288.</p></details></li>
</ol>

<div class="lx-fp-tabw"><table class="lx-fp-tab b3-ptab"><caption class="lx-sr">The solved plan, MW, by plant and hour</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">MW</th><th scope="col">18:00</th><th scope="col">19:00</th><th scope="col">20:00</th><th scope="col">21:00</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">nuclear</th><td class="n">100</td><td class="n">100</td><td class="n">100</td><td class="n">100</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">wind</th><td class="n">59</td><td class="n">72</td><td class="n">89</td><td class="n">98</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">solar</th><td class="n">70</td><td class="n">14</td><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">combined-cycle</th><td class="n">105</td><td class="n">145</td><td class="n">130</td><td class="n">105</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">peaker</th><td class="n">10</td><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">unserved</th><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">demand</th><td class="n">344</td><td class="n">331</td><td class="n">319</td><td class="n">303</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<ul class="b3-static-worked"><li><b>Balance at 18:00.</b> 100 + 59 + 70 + 105 + 10 = 344 MW, the demand ✓</li><li><b>Nuclear.</b> 400 MWh × $10 = $4,000</li><li><b>Combined-cycle.</b> 485 MWh × $40 = $19,400</li></ul>
<p>Peaker cost? Total, by hand?</p>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Peaker $1,000. $24,400, the solver's objective too: the model's cost and a hand count agree.</p></details></li>
<li><p><b>Check the solar dip, 14:00 to 17:00</b> (from scratch, about 7 min)</p>
<p>The combined-cycle plant starts from 45 MW at 13:00, lesson 0's cheapest-first plan.</p>
<div class="lx-fp-tabw"><table class="lx-fp-tab b3-ptab"><caption class="lx-sr">The solved plan, MW, by plant and hour</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">MW</th><th scope="col">14:00</th><th scope="col">15:00</th><th scope="col">16:00</th><th scope="col">17:00</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">nuclear</th><td class="n">100</td><td class="n">100</td><td class="n">100</td><td class="n">100</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">wind</th><td class="n">33</td><td class="n">37</td><td class="n">47</td><td class="n">54</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">solar</th><td class="n">112</td><td class="n">147</td><td class="n">161</td><td class="n">130</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">combined-cycle</th><td class="n">85</td><td class="n">60</td><td class="n">45</td><td class="n">65</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">peaker</th><td class="n">10</td><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">unserved</th><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td><td class="n">0</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">demand</th><td class="n">340</td><td class="n">344</td><td class="n">353</td><td class="n">349</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p>Supply at 14:00? Cost by hand, all four hours? Your guess for the 14:00 balance dual?</p>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Balanced (340 MW), $15,200 by hand, the solver's objective, and a $100 dual: the peaker is the marginal plant at 14:00. The solver's balance duals: 14:00 $100, 15:00 $40, 16:00 $40 and 17:00 $40 per MWh.</p></details></li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-fp-foot">The models are this lesson's dispatch of 3 September 2025, solved by HiGHS in your browser (a precomputed answer if it cannot load). The 65 MW and 45 MW starts are lesson 0's cheapest-first plan at 17:00 and 13:00; the storage and reserve lines are illustrative.</p>
```
